historical significance led us to what we see today a thought on how we got from the civil rights era to today without naming parties or people one thing i dont think we talk about enough is how power actually moved through generations in the us the kids who protested desegregation during the civil rights movement didnt disappear they grew up many became ceos judges politicians police chiefs prosecutors school administrators and corporate leaders legal integration happened but cultural reconciliation largely didnt beliefs didnt evaporate just because laws changed instead of explicit segregation systems evolved redlining became market forces jim crow became law and order racial control became the war on drugs poverty became criminalized schools increasingly mirrored factory schedules and later prison pipelines wealth accumulated upward while opportunity narrowed downward none of this required overt racism anymore it worked through policy zoning education sentencing and economic design all framed as neutral fast forward a few decades and you get a country where the middle class is hollowed out debt replaces stability housing healthcare and education become luxury goods surveillance expands quietly algorithms trained on biased data automate inequality then obama is elected for the first time political power visibly shifts in a way that challenges longstanding identity assumptions that moment didnt just change policy debates it triggered an identity crisis for many americans who had never processed integration emotionally only legally from there backlash politics isnt really about taxes or borders its about restoring certainty hierarchy and a sense of control in a system that feels like it stopped working for some and never worked for others what were seeing today didnt start with one politician or one election its the result of unresolved history inherited power and systems that adapte stead of transformed you dont have to agree with this but if we keep treating todays conflict as sudden or personality driven well never understand why it feels so permanent

a look at the history of political protest in the united states can it still effect change in a changing world like many americans in 2025 i found myself standing on the street or marching down a street or on the grounds of my state capital waving signs chanting slogans and listening to speakers talking about what was going on in this country also like many americans in 2025 this was the first time in my life i had been upset enough about what was happening in this country to actually get out there and try to do something about the hands off rally put on by 50501 in early april was the first one i attended there was another 50501 event in april and then a no kings rally in june and again in october i attended them all i loved that the crowds were getting bigger and bigger every time and really thought that would get our elected officials attention and make a difference shortly after the first no kings rally i began to realize that it wasnt making a difference i was thrilled that so many people were like me feeling the need to do something but the fact that nothing was getting better and if anything things were getting worse in my opinion was maddening i needed to know what the next step was how do we take this tremendous momentum that has started and turn it into a force to effect change in a nonviolent way i have always been a history buff and a bit of a writer so i thought of how this country began pamphlets calling for change in the american colonies were a huge force leading up to the revolutionary war it took me a while to figure all this out but after the october no kings rally i turned to todays version of the pamphlet social media i put up my first post i described what happened at the rally how great it was that so many people were there and i stressed how this alone would not make a difference and that we could not let it pacify us we needed to harness this momentum and figure out what the next step should be the post got about 5000 views and 100 comments in 24 hours nothing i know but i dont think i had ever had 5000 people combined in my entire life paying attention to what i had to say it inspired me i have created probably 30 40 posts in the last three months in several different places i have seen anywhere from just a few hundred views to almost 15 million most of my posts have been political in nature and while i do get support for my ideas a recurring thought that i see in the comments left is that nothing will change protesting is a waste of time it never works and it never has i take exception to this idea the history of this country is full of examples of protests making a difference while the pamphlets mentioned above did not in and of themselves lead to americas independence from great britain they did raise awareness of the issues among the colonists which led to events such as the boston tea party and eventually the american revolutionary war some examples from american history of peaceful protest leading to policy change in the united states include the womens suffrage movement 1850s1920 the montgomery bus boycott 19551956 martin luther kings march on washington 1963 the selma alabama marches 1965 and the vietnam war protests late 1960searly 1970s while these protests all had different goals or policies that they were trying to change the movements did have several common denominators the change did not come quickly participants in these movements had to be dedicated to their cause and had to devote a lot of time and personal resources to it getting to the goal required considerable amounts of personal sacrifice either physically emotionally economically or a combination of elements from people participating in the movement causes that could incorporate an economic impact on the powers in charge seemed to achieve their goals faster such as the montgomery bus boycott or more recently the boycott of disney over the suspension of jimmy kimmel my question for you is do you agree with so many of the respondents to my posts is protesting a waste of time that never changes anything or does it still serve a purpose in effecting change even in todays changing world as always thank you for your contributions

education department pauses wage seizures for unpaid student loans the education department has paused its efforts to seize wages and tax refunds from borrowers in default on their student loans education secretary linda mcmahon told local reporters in rhode island earlier this week that the education departments efforts to garnish wages on defaulted borrowers was put on pause for a bit the department confirmed this unexpected news in a press release friday the secretary did not elaborate on why garnishment was paused and blamed the previous administration for causing confusion among borrowers there is a pause on that at the moment mcmahon told the rhode island reporters during the previous administration i think the whole repayment of loan issues became just so confusing people just stopped paying this is a surprising reversal from the department which just announced that it sent the first notices about garnishing wages to about 1000 borrowers the week of jan 7 and that the notices would scale up on a month to month basis the white house senior staff at the education department and treasury have been engaging in discussions about collections on wages and tax refunds for unpaid student loans for months scott buchanan executive director of student loan servicing alliance an industry trade group said in an email obtained by politico affordability issues are viewed as core items for midterm elections by both parties he said there is obviously political awareness about those collection efforts and perceived impacts on those midterm elections and as such there has been much debate about how to handle things balancing the need to protect the federal fiscal interest and the impacts upon those struggling with loan obligations and politics the department said the temporary delay will enable the agency to implement new repayment plans created in the gops sweeping domestic policy bill while giving borrowers in default additional time to evaluate these new repayment options the department determined that involuntary collection efforts such as administrative wage garnishment and the treasury offset program will function more efficiently and fairly after the trump administration implements significant improvements to our broken student loan system undersecretary of education nicholas kent said this would have been the first time in about five years that borrowers would see part of their pay withheld for unpaid federal student loans in march 2020 the agency paused payments and collections during the pandemic but now more than 5 million borrowers are considered in default on their loans education department officials announced in the spring their plans to start garnishing borrowers wages for pastdue student loan payments but it was unclear when they would start the trump administration also started the process of collecting on defaulted loans may 5 by withholding federal tax returns and social security benefits however the department eventually walked back its decision to garnish social security benefits advocacy groups have been urging the department to hold off on garnishing wages during a time when the cost of housing food and other everyday needs has skyrocketed the decision to resume wage garnishment of millions of borrowers amidst a growing affordability crisis crushing working families is calloused and unnecessary protect borrowers and other advocacy groups wrote the decision also comes at a time when struggling borrowers have been forced to wait amidst a nearly 1 million application backlog to enroll in an incomedriven repayment idr plan wage garnishment is also a complicated system that involves working with the borrowers employer to withhold the wages borrowers are considered to be in default after 270 days of missed payments collections generally take place after 360 days and the department is legally required to notify borrowers 30 days before their wages are garnished a student loan borrower in default could see up to 15 percent of their disposable pay withheld to collect on their debt until the loan is paid in full or default status is resolved

best pmi for maternity complications and caesarean delivery hi all i see questions about maternity cover pop up here fairly often and there seems to be a lot of confusion about whats actually included ive been looking into the specifics and thought a summary of the key principles might be helpful for anyone planning a family the most important thing to understand is that standard uk pmi does not cover routine pregnancy or childbirth insurers view pregnancy as a natural life event not an unforeseen medical condition this means routine scans antenatal appointments and a standard delivery are not covered where pmi can provide a safety net is with unexpected complications that arise during pregnancy or childbirth these are treated as acute medical conditions which is what pmi is designed for insurers have specific lists of what they define as a complication but they often include preeclampsia gestational diabetes ectopic pregnancy postpartum haemorrhage severe 3rd or 4th degree perineal tears requiring surgical repair another major point of confusion is around caesareans a csection you choose to have for nonmedical reasons elective is never covered however a csection that is deemed medically necessary by a consultant for the health of the mother or baby often called an emergency csection is typically the kind of event that can be covered under the complications benefit its also crucial to remember the rules around preexisting conditions if you have a condition before taking out your policy like chronic high blood pressure and it gets worse during pregnancy that wont be covered the cover is for new acute conditions that arise after your policy starts full disclosure these insights are from a guide i work on for those who have had pmi during pregnancy did you find the complications cover useful or were there any unexpected hurdles in the claims process
